explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates LLM-as-a-judge against human evaluation by reporting Pearson correlation scores between LLM judgments and human annotations, comparing them on the same set of instances.

prompts.notes: The paper states the prompt was crafted to be as close as possible to the human annotation instructions, but the exact prompt text is not provided in the given text.

guidelines.notes: Human annotators spot and highlight accuracy errors on word level using four error categories (incorrect, not checkable, misleading, other). Detailed instructions are in Appendix C.

sample_size.notes: Human evaluation was conducted on 50 tables per benchmark. The correlation is measured across models and datasets.

quantitative_scores.notes: Correlation between TAPAS metric and human evaluation

Correlation between LLM-as-a-judge with Llama 3.3 70B and human evaluation across models and datasets

correlation_interpretation.interpretation: LLM-as-a-judge shows moderate correlation; TAPAS/TAPEX show low correlation

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-as-a-judge with Llama 3.3 70B shows moderate correlation (0.53) with human evaluation, while automatic metrics TAPAS and TAPEX show only low correlation (0.12 and 0.11), indicating LLM judges are more reliable.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM-as-a-judge and human evaluation use the same four error categories: incorrect, not checkable, misleading, and other.
